name: Chicken Fried Rice
cuisine: Indo-Chinese (Mumbai street, "Chinese gaadi" and restaurant style)

ingredients.name: Basmati rice (raw), or cooked leftover rice
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅓ cup raw, or about 1⅓ cups cooked

ingredients.name: Water, for boiling the rice (only if cooking from raw)
Chicken, boneless (breast or thigh)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 1 small breast, cut into thin strips (about ¾ cup)

ingredients.name: Light soy sauce
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (½ tsp in the marinade, 1½ tsp in the rice)

ingredients.name: Black pepper powder (kali mirch), or white pepper
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ tsp (a pinch in the marinade, the rest in the rice)

ingredients.name: Refined groundnut or sunflower oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2½ tsp (1 tsp chicken, ½ tsp egg, 1 tsp vegetables)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium onion, thinly sliced or diced

ingredients.name: Spring onion (hara pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 stalks: whites chopped, greens sliced separately

ingredients.name: Carrot (gajar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ cup, finely diced or thin strips

ingredients.name: Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅛ tsp (soy sauce is already salty; a pinch goes in the marinade)

equipment: Wok or heavy iron kadai (24–28 cm)
Large saucepan and a colander/strainer, for boiling rice from raw (skip with leftover rice)
Large plate or tray, to spread and cool the rice
Chopping board and a sharp knife
3 small bowls (marinated chicken, beaten egg, sauce mix) and 1 plate for the cooked chicken and egg
Wide flat spatula or wok ladle (jhara/kadchi)
Fork or whisk, for beating the egg
Measuring spoons (a normal teaspoon is fine) and a kitchen scale if you have one; without a scale, use the household measures in section 2

steps.title: Rinse the rice (skip if using leftover rice)
steps.text: Rinse 65 g (⅓ cup) basmati in a bowl of water 3 times, until the water is almost clear.
steps.tip: Rinsing removes surface starch, which keeps fried rice from turning sticky.
steps.visualCue: Water is only slightly cloudy
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling rice in water, cloudy water poured off.

steps.title: Boil the rice
steps.text: Bring about 700 ml water to a rolling boil, add the rice, and boil uncovered.
steps.tip: Slightly undercooked is right; the rice cooks a little more in the wok.
steps.visualCue: A grain pressed between fingers is soft outside with a tiny firm centre (about 90% cooked)
steps.cameraCheck: A grain squeezed between two fingers
steps.videoShot: Rice dancing in boiling water, a grain lifted on a spoon.

steps.title: Drain the rice
steps.text: Tip the rice into the colander and let the water drain fully.
steps.visualCue: Steam rising, no water dripping
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the colander
steps.videoShot: Rice pouring into a colander with a burst of steam.

steps.title: Spread and cool the rice
steps.text: Spread the rice in a thin layer on a large plate. Cool uncovered, then refrigerate if you have time.
steps.tip: Using leftover rice? Take 200 g (about 1⅓ cups) from the fridge and break up any lumps with your fingers; that is this step done.
steps.visualCue: Grains are cool to the touch, dry on the surface and separate
steps.cameraCheck: The rice spread on the plate
steps.videoShot: A fork fluffing rice across a plate.

steps.title: Slice the chicken
steps.text: Cut 100 g boneless chicken into thin strips or small cubes, about 1 cm thick.
steps.tip: Wash the board and knife with soap afterwards, before cutting vegetables.
steps.visualCue: Even, thin pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced chicken on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife slicing chicken into strips.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the chicken with ½ tsp soy sauce, a pinch of pepper, a pinch of salt and 1 tsp cornflour.
steps.tip: The cornflour coat keeps the chicken soft on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Each piece has a thin, even coating with no dry powder
steps.cameraCheck: The coated chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Fingers or a spoon tossing chicken in cornflour.

steps.title: Chop garlic, ginger and chilli
steps.text: Finely chop 2–3 garlic cloves, ½-inch ginger and 1 green chilli.
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The small heap on the board
steps.videoShot: Rocking knife over garlic and ginger.

steps.title: Chop the onion and spring onion
steps.text: Slice ¼ onion (30 g). Chop the spring onion whites; slice the greens and keep them apart.
steps.visualCue: Two separate heaps: whites with onion, greens alone
steps.cameraCheck: Both heaps on the board
steps.videoShot: Spring onion greens sliced into thin rings.

steps.title: Chop the hard vegetables
steps.text: Finely dice 30 g carrot and 25 g French beans.
steps.tip: Small pieces cook in the same 2 minutes as the rest; big pieces stay raw.
steps.visualCue: Pieces about the size of a rice grain to a pea
steps.cameraCheck: The carrot and beans in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Beans lined up and chopped across.

steps.title: Chop the soft vegetables
steps.text: Shred 30 g cabbage finely and dice 25 g capsicum.
steps.visualCue: Fine green shreds and small capsicum squares
steps.cameraCheck: The cabbage and capsicum in a bowl
steps.videoShot: The knife shredding cabbage.

steps.title: Make the sauce mix
steps.text: In a small cup, mix 1½ tsp soy sauce, ½ tsp vinegar, ¼ tsp sugar and the remaining pepper.
steps.visualCue: A small cup of dark liquid with the sugar dissolved
steps.cameraCheck: The sauce cup
steps.videoShot: Soy sauce poured into a cup, vinegar following.

steps.title: Beat the egg
steps.text: Crack 1 egg into a bowl and beat with a fork.
steps.visualCue: Evenly yellow, a few bubbles
steps.cameraCheck: The beaten egg
steps.videoShot: A fork whisking an egg.

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Put the wok on high heat and add 1 tsp oil.
steps.tip: Keep everything chopped and within reach from now on; the rest moves fast.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and swirls easily, a faint wisp of smoke
steps.cameraCheck: The oil in the wok
steps.videoShot: Oil being swirled around a hot wok.

steps.title: Spread the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken in one layer and leave it untouched.
steps.visualCue: A loud sizzle; the underside turns white and lightly golden
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken in one layer
steps.videoShot: Chicken strips hitting the hot wok.

steps.title: Stir-fry the chicken
steps.text: Toss and cook until done all the way through.
steps.tip: If the pan is crowded and liquid pools, turn the heat up and wait; it should fry, not boil.
steps.visualCue: White throughout with golden edges; a cut piece has no pink inside
steps.cameraCheck: A piece of chicken cut open
steps.videoShot: Chicken tossed in the wok, one piece cut in half.

steps.title: Take out the chicken
steps.text: Lift the chicken onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Wok empty with a thin film of oil left
steps.cameraCheck: The cooked chicken on the plate
steps.videoShot: Chicken lifted out with the spatula.

steps.title: Scramble the egg
steps.text: Add ½ tsp oil, pour in the egg, and stir until just set in soft curds.
steps.visualCue: Soft yellow curds, no runny liquid
steps.cameraCheck: The scrambled egg in the wok
steps.videoShot: Egg setting and broken up with the spatula.

steps.title: Take out the egg
steps.text: Put the egg on the plate with the chicken.
steps.visualCue: Wok almost clean
steps.cameraCheck: Chicken and egg on the plate
steps.videoShot: Egg pushed onto the plate.

steps.title: Fry garlic, ginger and chilli
steps.text: Add 1 tsp oil, then the chopped garlic, ginger and green chilli. Stir on high heat.
steps.tip: Burnt garlic tastes bitter; if it goes dark brown, wipe the wok and redo this step.
steps.visualCue: Strong garlic smell, garlic just turning pale gold (not brown)
steps.cameraCheck: The garlic in the oil
steps.videoShot: Garlic sizzling in the wok.

steps.title: Add onion and spring onion whites
steps.text: Stir-fry on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Onion edges turn translucent but still crisp
steps.cameraCheck: The onion in the wok
steps.videoShot: Onion tossed through the garlic.

steps.title: Add carrot and beans
steps.text: Stir-fry on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Carrot turns bright orange, beans bright green
steps.cameraCheck: The vegetables in the wok
steps.videoShot: Carrot and beans tossed.

steps.title: Add cabbage and capsicum
steps.text: Stir-fry on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Cabbage just wilted at the edges, capsicum glossy and still crunchy
steps.cameraCheck: All the vegetables in the wok
steps.videoShot: Cabbage shreds tossed with a flip of the wok.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Add the 200 g cooled rice and toss so it mixes with the vegetables.
steps.tip: Press any lumps with the back of the spatula; don't mash.
steps.visualCue: Rice spread through the vegetables, no lumps
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the wok
steps.videoShot: Rice tipped into the wok and broken up.

steps.title: Add the sauce mix
steps.text: Pour the sauce cup around the hot edge of the wok, not in the centre, and toss.
steps.visualCue: Rice turns an even light brown; a quick sizzle and toasty smell at the edge
steps.cameraCheck: The evenly coloured rice
steps.videoShot: Sauce poured around the wok edge, steam rising.

steps.title: Return the chicken and egg
steps.text: Add the chicken and egg back and toss on high heat.
steps.visualCue: Chicken and egg pieces spread through, everything steaming hot
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed fried rice
steps.videoShot: Chicken tumbling back into the rice.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste a spoonful and add the ⅛ tsp salt only if it needs it.
steps.tip: Add more pepper or vinegar before more soy sauce; it keeps sodium down.
steps.visualCue: Lightly seasoned, not salty
steps.cameraCheck: The spoon of rice
steps.videoShot: A spoon lifting rice to taste.

steps.title: Finish with spring onion greens
steps.text: Turn off the heat, add the spring onion greens and toss once.
steps.visualCue: Bright green rings throughout
steps.cameraCheck: The finished fried rice in the wok
steps.videoShot: Spring onion greens scattered and tossed.

steps.title: Plate it
steps.text: Transfer to a plate and serve hot.
steps.visualCue: Separate, glossy grains with chicken, egg and vegetables visible
steps.cameraCheck: The finished plate
steps.videoShot: Fried rice heaped on a plate, steam rising.

reasons: the home plate gives about 37 g protein from lean chicken and an egg, about 170 g vegetables and only 2½ tsp oil, with nothing deep-fried and almost no added sugar. Points come off for refined white rice as the base (about 52 g carbs from rice alone), sodium around 1,050 mg (over half the daily limit, mostly soy sauce) and about 260 mg cholesterol from the egg yolk. Restaurant plates commonly use 2–3 tbsp oil, more soy sauce, salt and MSG (sodium often well over 1,500 mg, est.), fewer vegetables and less chicken relative to rice; the one published restaurant figure (Chinese Wok) shows 26 g fat and only 22 g protein.

researchRating.basis: chicken fried rice is one of India's most-ordered dishes: Swiggy's StatEATistics reports listed it 4th among the most-loved dishes in 2019 and 3rd among the top-ordered dishes in 2022 (behind only chicken biryani and masala dosa), and BloombergQuint's coverage of Swiggy's 2021 report named it among Mumbai's top orders. It is on almost every Indo-Chinese, "Chinese gaadi" and dhaba-Chinese menu in Mumbai, and home-cooking blogs (Cooking and Me, Raksha's Kitchen, Recipes Are Simple, Ruchik Randhap, Indiaphile) and chefs (Ranveer Brar's Mumbai-style chicken chopper rice, Sanjeev Kapoor's chicken triple fried rice) all publish it. Small deduction because individual recipe ratings were sparse in the sources found, and a common complaint is greasy, over-salted, mushy restaurant versions.

storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; keep in a closed box in the fridge for up to 1 day (cooked rice can carry *Bacillus cereus* spores, so fridge time is kept short). Freezer: up to 1 month in a flat zip bag. Reheat only once, in a hot pan with 1 tbsp water, tossing for 3–4 minutes until steaming hot all through, or microwave covered with a splash of water for 2 minutes, stirring halfway. Do not leave it at room temperature overnight.
leftoverRemix: Mumbai-style "omelette fried rice". Beat 1 egg with a pinch of salt and pepper, pour it into a hot greased pan and swirl into a thin omelette. Put a cup of reheated chicken fried rice on one half, add a spoon of Schezwan chutney and spring onion, fold the omelette over and serve in wedges with ketchup. The leftover rice becomes a new, egg-wrapped dish.
burnOff: about 8.7 km of running (610 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 12.2 km of brisk walking (about 2 hours 25 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: contains chicken, egg, rice, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided in the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: rice is the grain most strictly avoided on Ekadashi, and the dish also has chicken, egg, onion and garlic.

jain.reason: contains chicken and egg, plus onion, garlic, ginger and carrot.

ramadan.reason: use halal chicken; good for iftar, but for sehri cut the soy sauce to 1 tsp because the salt drives thirst during the fast.

jain.reason: contains chicken and egg, plus onion, garlic, ginger and carrot (root vegetables); see the Jain veg fried rice variant.

vegan.reason: contains chicken and egg; see the tofu fried rice variant.

sattvik.reason: contains onion, spring onion and garlic, and chicken and egg are not sattvik foods; onion and garlic can be skipped for taste, but that does not make the dish sattvik.

glutenFree.reason: regular soy sauce is brewed with wheat; use a certified gluten-free tamari and check the cornflour label (maize, but may be processed with wheat). No hing is used.

dairyFree.reason: no milk, curd, butter, ghee, cream or paneer.

description: A non-veg, dairy-free Indo-Chinese chicken-and-egg fried rice, high in protein; vegetarian, Jain, vegan, gluten-free and low-oil versions below.
